findings.description: No line in tests/apps.bats has [[ or (( as its first non-whitespace token; the grep exits 1 (no match) rather than 2 (failed to run), and the baseline's grep -oE bracket expression at line 50 was left byte-identical.
findings.evidence:
$ /usr/bin/grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(\[\[|\(\()' tests/apps.bats; echo "EXIT=$?"
EXIT=1
(no stdout; exit 1 = no match, not the exit-2 blocked case)

Baseline line 50 vs working-tree line 52 (shifted +2 by the added load line), compared as bytes in python:
baseline line 50: b'    grep -oE \'\\{ name = "[^"]+", *type = "[^"]+", *bundles = \\[[^]]*\\] \\}\' "$FIXTURE/.chezmoidata.toml" \\'
worktree line 52: b'    grep -oE \'\\{ name = "[^"]+", *type = "[^"]+", *bundles = \\[[^]]*\\] \\}\' "$FIXTURE/.chezmoidata.toml" \\'
line 50 UNCHANGED: True

registry_line therefore still works, which the 5 dependent conversions confirm at runtime (all 18 cases ok, below).

findings.description: All 11 conversions keep the baseline needle byte-for-byte, keep the haystack, and keep polarity (== to assert_contains, no assert_not_contains introduced); the five registry_line sites all pass their computed haystack as the helper's second argument with the original registry_line argument intact.
findings.evidence:
$ git show 61213fe:tests/apps.bats > /tmp/apps-baseline.bats && diff /tmp/apps-baseline.bats tests/apps.bats
12a13,14
> load 'helpers'
>
135c137
< \t[[ "$(registry_line 'owner/repo/x')" == *'bundles = ["media"]'* ]]
---
> \tassert_contains 'bundles = ["media"]' "$(registry_line 'owner/repo/x')"
(...11 conversions total, plus the load line; no other hunks, so nothing else in the file moved)

Byte-equality re-derived mechanically rather than by eye: for each site I sliced the baseline needle literal out from between '== *' and '* ]]' (quotes included) and compared the converted line against the reconstruction b'\tassert_contains ' + needle + b' "$(' + haystack + b')"'.

Five registry_line sites (baseline -> worktree):
  135->137 BYTE-IDENTICAL=True  needle b'bundles = ["media"]'  arg 'owner/repo/x'
  142->144 BYTE-IDENTICAL=True  needle b'["cloud"]'  arg spotify
  143->145 BYTE-IDENTICAL=True  needle b'["cloud"]'  arg 1password
  150->152 BYTE-IDENTICAL=True  needle b'bundles = ["core", "media"]'  arg spotify
  190->192 BYTE-IDENTICAL=True  needle b'{ name = "yq", type = "brew", bundles = ["core"] },'  arg yq (trailing comma present)
ALL FIVE OK: True

Six $output sites, single-argument form, needles unchanged:
  179->181 b'"found 0"' OK=True
  202->204 b'"nothing untracked"' OK=True
  274->276 b'"fzf"' OK=True
  280->282 b'"unknown option"' OK=True
  286->288 b'"--adopt"' OK=True
  287->289 b'"--machine"' OK=True

Helper still carries the -- guard, so the two needles starting with -- are safe (tests/helpers.bash:7-10):
  assert_contains() {
  \tlocal needle="$1" haystack="${2-$output}"
  \tgrep -qF -- "$needle" <<<"$haystack"
  }

Discriminating probe under /bin/bash 3.2.57(1)-release, proving the conversions are live rather than tautological and that the second argument is honored (a dropped haystack would silently re-point at $output):
  $ output='bundles = ["media"]'   # would pass if the 2nd arg were ignored
  assert_contains 'bundles = ["media"]' 'SOMETHING ELSE'  -> 1  (2nd arg honored)
  assert_contains '--adopt' 'usage: --adopt --machine'    -> 0  (-- guard works)
  yq needle vs line WITH comma                            -> 0
  yq needle vs same line WITHOUT comma                    -> 1  (comma is load-bearing)

No helper call inlines its own comparison; every converted site calls assert_contains by name.
